_: The escalation register [R-IND-01]. Every question that has reached the principal, with the routes actually run before it left the room, the refs actually searched, what was done meanwhile, and the default that fires if no answer comes. scripts/check_escalations.py reads it from outside and RE-CHECKS each open entry against every live ref, so an entry cannot go on asking for something already supplied.

entries.question: The 10-year Egyptian government bond yield and the CBE overnight deposit rate at each year-end 2013-2023, for the point-in-time macro archive [R-VCAL-01].

routes.route: cbe.org.eg statistics pages and static PDF paths
routes.outcome: HTTP 200 with a 269-byte 'Request Rejected' body on every path
404 bot-protection page for every series id
host does not resolve; api.imf.org rejects the IFS dataflow

reachable and read, but the only rate row is a FISCAL-YEAR AVERAGE of a 3-month bill where the house discounts on a 10-year year-end yield. Recording it would be an instrument substitution wearing the right field name.

routes.route: web.archive.org snapshot of the CBE statistics pages

entries.why_only_the_principal: Both are OBSERVED figures, so this is pure access and not a point-in-time problem. Every free route refuses at the proxy; the principal holds the CBE / Ministry of Finance export.
entries.done_meanwhile: The archive's other four required figures were sourced point-in-time (ERP and default spread from the Damodaran vintages published AT each origin, inflation from six IMF WEO editions published before their origins), so the archive was complete except for these two and closed the moment they arrived.
entries.default_if_no_answer: Drop every origin that lacks them and shorten the window — never interpolate, never carry a neighbouring year.
entries.note: THE CASE THIS RULE WAS WRITTEN FOR. The principal supplied both series on the morning of 3 September and one supplied figure was found wrong and corrected against the CBE decision record. Six origins went live. Hours later this session ASKED FOR THEM AGAIN, because it read main and the answer was on the calibration session's branch. The gate now re-checks this entry's marker across every live ref on every run, so the same re-ask goes RED instead of reaching the principal.

entries.question: A fresh OHLC export for the EGX names whose libraries stop at 6 August 2026 — ARCC, AMOC, EGCH and the others listed by the gap gate's price basis. Without it the house's LATEST KNOWN price is four weeks old and [R-GAP-01] cannot audit a gap it cannot see.

routes.route: the persistent library itself, engine/raw_ohlc/EG/*.csv, read newest-first
routes.outcome: ARCC, AMOC and EGCH stop at 06-08-2026; TMGH and PHDC reach 23-08-2026. Confirmed by reading the files, not a manifest.

routes.route: the principal's own figures, supplied in chat 03-09-2026
routes.outcome: ARCC 76.81 and AMOC 13.43 at 01-09, against library closes of 59.00 and 9.10 — moves of +30.2% and +47.6% the library never saw. Recorded as evidence of the gap, NOT written into the library: a price typed from a chat message is not a vendor export and would enter a calibration panel as one.

routes.route: every free web route to EGX closes, as recorded for the CBE series
routes.outcome: the same proxy refusals; and a price series assembled from a rendered page is not the vendor format the libraries and Step 0.0 expect.

entries.why_only_the_principal: The OHLC libraries are supplied by the principal's own vendor export and always have been; this is the same shape of file they already send. No route available here produces one.
entries.done_meanwhile: The gap gate was re-pointed at the latest known price per its own rule text rather than at the spot each study froze at strike, and it now prints the age of the library it compared against, so a stale comparison reports as stale instead of passing in silence. The finding on ARCC and AMOC is recorded with its arithmetic.
entries.default_if_no_answer: Continue on the 6-August library and state its date wherever a gap is quoted; do NOT type the supplied prices into the library, and do not audit ARCC or AMOC at a price the house cannot date.
entries.resolves_when_note: the 1 September 2026 session, the date the principal's own quoted price carries. The first marker written here was '/2026', which the file already contained — the gate refused it immediately, which is the clause this register exists for working on the person writing the register.

entries.question: Electro Cable Egypt (EGX: ELEC) audited financial statements — FY2023, FY2024 and every disclosed 2025 period (Q1, H1, 9M), consolidated where issued and standalone otherwise. The company's own website LISTS all of them and SERVES none of them; without them SIGCM clause 1 blocks this study outright, because its entire income statement and balance sheet currently rest on data vendors and press.

routes.route: the company's own website, www.ececables.com — homepage, investor-relations, shareholder-structure and the financial-statements index
routes.outcome: HTTP 200 on every page. THE STUDY'S RECORDED REASON ('the egress proxy blocked the company website') IS FALSE as of today and was re-tested rather than believed [R-ENF-04]. The index lists ~60 audited statements.

routes.route: every statement PDF the index links, and the same URLs as the WordPress media API returns them
routes.outcome: HTTP 404 on all of them. Not an encoding problem: a non-Arabic PDF in the same tree 404s too, while a 2020-vintage asset in that tree returns 200 — so the host serves the path and not the files. Everything uploaded after August 2020 is listed and unserved.

routes.route: the legacy host ece.allmediaegypt.com, which carries the 2015-2020 statements
a real browser (Chromium via Playwright) against the same pages, in case the index or the files were rendered rather than served
routes.outcome: the tunnel resets before navigation; curl reaches the same pages fine, so the browser adds nothing here and the 404s are the origin's, not a rendering problem.

routes.route: the EGX disclosure portal — www.egx.com.eg, disclosure.egx.com.eg, mist.com.eg
routes.outcome: tunnel closed mid-exchange on nine attempts across three hosts. The proxy's own status endpoint records data received before the close, so it is a relay failure rather than a policy denial. Reported, not routed around.

routes.route: every live ref of this repository, for a filing committed on another branch
routes.outcome: only the research note exists on any ref; no ELEC filing anywhere.

entries.why_only_the_principal: Pure access, and every free route is exhausted: the issuer publishes an index it does not serve, its old host is gone, and the exchange is unreachable through the relay. The principal has supplied primary filings before when a company site refused (the ARCC precedent, which this protocol records as the rule working rather than failing).
entries.done_meanwhile: ELEC's committed numbers were audited as far as vendor data allows and the findings written to engine/elec_study/SOURCE_BLOCK_04-09-2026.md: the retired g x IC terminal (return on capital 583bp BELOW its own cost of capital, 54.5% of profit reinvested at that spread), a terminal growth rate that is -1.87% real and stated nowhere, and terminal invested capital resting on a typed 0.05-of-revenue constant. Each is priced. The study stays HELD and no delivered figure was moved, because moving one would build further on the base that is the problem.
entries.default_if_no_answer: WITHDRAW ELEC FROM COVERAGE rather than re-issue it on aggregator data. A study nobody can source is not a study with a wide range; it is not a study. Withdrawal removes the name from the book and leaves the directory with this record in it.
entries.note: The correction this entry carries is not that the documents are unobtainable — they are — but that the RECORDED REASON was wrong for a month, and a wrong reason is actionable in the wrong direction: 'the proxy blocked it' invites trying again, 'the issuer does not serve its own archive' does not.

entries.question: [R-LENS-03]'s LENS_REGISTRY is a CLOSED enumeration keyed on the lessons register's own class list, and a study must map into one of its thirteen rows to publish a lens record. SAVOLA — food manufacturing, grocery retail and a listed quick-service stake — maps to none of them, and BOTH available routes are barred by rules this house already holds. Adding a row is barred because the rule says in terms that a class is added when a DIFFERENT LENS carries the weight and never merely when the industry differs, and a grocer's lens set is identical to three rows already there (primary cash flow; cross-checks own-history EV/EBITDA, a relative multiple and book). Mapping it to one of those rows is barred because a name resolving to the wrong subject is worse than an absence — calling a supermarket group a telecom operator would put that label in the study's own record. So SAVOLA cannot retire its typed 45/25/15/15 blend under [R-LENS-03] without one of the two being decided.

routes.route: research_protocol.LENS_REGISTRY and lessons_register.CLASSES, read live and compared — the registry asserts on the class list at import, so the two cannot be changed independently
routes.outcome: 13 classes; three rows (telecom operator, airline, pharmaceutical manufacturer) carry an IDENTICAL lens set. The duplication is the evidence: the registry keys on an industry NAME while the thing it stores is a lens SET.

routes.route: every study directory's committed lens_record, for a precedent mapping an operating company to a row named for another industry
routes.outcome: none — every conforming study's declared class matches its actual industry, so there is no house precedent for borrowing a row.

routes.route: the standing protocol and the digest, for what [R-LENS-03] says about a class that fits nothing
routes.outcome: The exemplar clause covers the analogous case for REPORTS ('adapt the nearest pattern's lens inside the skeleton and say which and why') and the registry clause does not carry the equivalent for CLASSES. The gap is in the rule, not in the study.

routes.route: research_protocol.LENS_REGISTRY read against a SECOND name that meets the same wall — EMPOWER, a regulated district-cooling utility on the DFM
routes.outcome: no row either, and the wall is the same one: a chilled-water network's lens set is a cash-flow primary cross-checked on its own EV/EBITDA history, a relative multiple and book — identical to the three duplicate rows already there — so adding a class would again be adding it for an INDUSTRY difference, which the rule forbids in terms. TWO INDEPENDENT NAMES IN ONE WEEK IS THE SECOND OBSERVATION [R-LESSON-01] asks for before widening a finding.

entries.why_only_the_principal: Both routes require changing a standing rule rather than applying one: either [R-LENS-03]'s bar on adding a class for an industry difference, or the taxonomy the lessons register and the lens registry share. A rule amendment is the principal's, and taking it inside a study rebuild is exactly the per-name exception this house forbids everywhere else.
entries.done_meanwhile: SAVOLA's two terminal levers were taken in full — growth stored as a real rate on the house Saudi path, and the terminal rebuilt through the sanctioned module on an asset life DERIVED by identity from note 6's own cost and depreciation columns. The blend is left standing and SAVOLA stays on the lens ratchet, where it already sat legitimately. The cost of leaving it is measured and stated rather than implied: the blend publishes 27.28 against a cash-flow lens of 25.02, so retiring it would move the central 8.3% DOWN and the gap against the latest price from -10.0% to -17.4%. EMPOWER meets the identical wall and is left standing for the identical reason: its terminal was rebuilt in full through the sanctioned module on a derived 28.10-year life, and its typed 50/20/15/15 blend stays, with the cost measured rather than implied — the blend publishes 1.8523 against a cash-flow lens of 2.1335, so retiring it would move the central 15.2% UP and the gap against the latest 1.57 from +18.0% to +35.9%. THE TWO NAMES MOVE IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS, which is the strongest evidence available that this is a taxonomy question and not a valuation one: on SAVOLA the blend flatters and on EMPOWER it discounts, so no answer to it can be chosen for the number it produces.
entries.default_if_no_answer: RENAME THE REGISTRY'S ROWS FOR THEIR LENS SETS RATHER THAN FOR INDUSTRIES, and merge the three duplicates into one row — an operating company valued on its own cash flows and cross-checked on its own EV/EBITDA history, a relative multiple and book. That is not adding a class for an industry: it is naming the registry for the thing it actually stores, which makes the closed enumeration closable. SAVOLA then maps to it without anybody inventing a fit.
entries.note: The gap is worth naming beyond this one name: the registry is keyed on an industry NAME and stores a lens SET, and three of its thirteen rows already store the same set. A taxonomy that must grow per industry, under a rule that forbids growing per industry, has no state in which a new operating company can be added — which is a property of the design rather than of any study that meets it. EMPOWER adds one thing the first instance could not show: its blend carries a NORMALISED EARNINGS lens at 15%, and normalised earnings appears in no row of the registry at all. So even under the default fix — rename the rows for their lens sets and merge the duplicates — that lens still has to go, which is the rule working as intended rather than a further gap in it.
